options.a: Administer TRELA and regulate Texas real estate license holders
options.b: Prosecute criminal real estate fraud cases in Texas district courts
options.c: License and regulate Texas residential mortgage loan originators
options.d: Decide landlord-tenant and title disputes between Texas parties

distractorExplanations.b: Criminal prosecution belongs to district/county attorneys; TREC is an administrative licensing agency, not a prosecutor.
distractorExplanations.c: Mortgage loan originators are licensed by the Department of Savings and Mortgage Lending or OCCC, not TREC.
distractorExplanations.d: Private landlord-tenant and title disputes are decided by justice and district courts; TREC only regulates license holders.

options.a: Go inactive but may close pending deals under the suspended broker
options.b: May keep practicing for 30 days under the suspended broker's name
options.c: Cannot continue practicing until sponsored by another active broker
options.d: May practice on their own sales agent license without a new sponsor

distractorExplanations.a: Once the sponsoring broker's license is suspended or revoked, sponsored agents go inactive and cannot keep closing deals under that broker.
distractorExplanations.b: There is no 30-day grace period; a sales agent cannot act under a broker whose license is suspended or revoked.
distractorExplanations.d: A Texas sales agent license only authorizes activity while sponsored by an active broker; it cannot be used independently.

options.a: Their commission split with the sponsoring broker and personal license history
options.b: Only the listing price history and days on market drawn from the MLS for comparable homes
options.c: The seller's disclosure notice contents, which the agent completes on the seller's behalf
options.d: Representation/agency status and required written information about brokerage services

distractorExplanations.a: The internal commission split and license history are not required consumer disclosures; representation and the IABS are.
distractorExplanations.b: Price history and days on market are marketing data, not the statutory representation and brokerage-services disclosure.
distractorExplanations.c: The seller's disclosure notice is the seller's own statement; agents should not complete it, and it is not the agent's disclosure duty.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-license-l.explanation: IABS and agency disclosures are core Texas practice requirements. These disclosures apply as required by the transaction.

options.a: Mixing client funds with broker personal/operating funds improperly
options.b: Spending client funds for the broker's own purposes without authorization
options.c: Depositing earnest money with a title company instead of the broker's trust account
options.d: Holding a buyer's earnest money in a separate trust account until closing

distractorExplanations.b: Spending client money for personal use is conversion, the next step beyond commingling, which is the mixing of funds itself.
distractorExplanations.c: Delivering earnest money to the escrow agent named in the contract is proper handling, not commingling.
distractorExplanations.d: Keeping client funds in a separate trust account is exactly what avoids commingling, so it cannot be the definition.

options.a: Draft the custom clauses, since license holders may prepare any lease for a client
options.b: Advise the client that an attorney may be needed; avoid unauthorized practice of law
options.c: Use the TREC promulgated residential lease, since TREC requires that form for all leases
options.d: Draft the clauses and have the sponsoring broker approve them before signing

distractorExplanations.a: License holders may only fill in promulgated or approved forms; drafting custom legal clauses is the unauthorized practice of law.
distractorExplanations.c: TREC does not promulgate a residential lease form; residential lease forms come from the Texas REALTORS® association.
distractorExplanations.d: Broker approval does not cure unauthorized practice of law; neither licensee may draft custom legal provisions.

options.a: Charging more than the maximum commission rate set by TREC for the county
options.b: Declining to join the local association of REALTORS® and the regional MLS
options.c: Dishonest conduct, misrepresentation, and other TRELA violations
options.d: Refusing to reduce the agreed commission after the seller asks for a lower fee

distractorExplanations.a: TREC does not set commission rates; commissions are negotiable between broker and client, so this is not a violation.
distractorExplanations.b: Association and MLS membership are voluntary private matters; TREC does not discipline for not joining them.
distractorExplanations.d: Holding a client to the negotiated commission is lawful; TREC discipline targets dishonesty and TRELA violations.

options.a: A sales agent who represents both parties without the sponsoring broker's consent
options.b: A title company escrow officer who holds the funds and closes for both parties
options.c: An attorney appointed by TREC to mediate disputes between buyers and sellers before closing
options.d: A broker who facilitates both parties with appointed licensees or without appointments

distractorExplanations.a: Only the broker can act as intermediary, and only with both parties' written consent; a sales agent cannot do it alone.
distractorExplanations.b: The escrow officer is a neutral closing agent, not a licensed broker in an intermediary brokerage relationship.
distractorExplanations.c: TREC does not appoint mediators; an intermediary is a broker working with both parties under TRELA.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-license-l.explanation: Intermediary practice is a Texas statutory brokerage relationship with strict disclosure/appointment rules. The appointment and disclosure rules are set by statute.

options.a: Show properties and answer questions about financing/terms as if negotiating the transaction
options.b: Place signs, order inspections, surveys, or repairs, and submit documents at the broker's direction
options.c: Schedule showing appointments and compile comparable-sales data for the agent's review
options.d: Deliver documents and enter listing data into the MLS under the broker's supervision

distractorExplanations.b: These are clerical and administrative tasks unlicensed assistants may perform under supervision, so they are not prohibited.
distractorExplanations.c: Scheduling and assembling data for a licensee are permitted clerical tasks; the prohibited act is negotiating or showing as an agent.
distractorExplanations.d: Delivering documents and data entry are routine support tasks that do not require a license.

options.a: Reimburse licensees for commissions that sellers refuse to pay at closing
options.b: Compensate aggrieved persons for certain unpaid judgments against licensees
options.c: Refund buyers' earnest money when an escrow title company becomes insolvent
options.d: Cover licensees' errors-and-omissions claims in place of E&O insurance

distractorExplanations.a: The fund protects consumers harmed by licensees, not licensees trying to collect unpaid commissions.
distractorExplanations.c: Title company insolvency is not covered; the fund pays unpaid judgments against license holders for TRELA-type misconduct.
distractorExplanations.d: The fund is not insurance for license holders; it pays aggrieved consumers and then pursues the licensee.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-license-l.explanation: The Real Estate Recovery Trust Account is a consumer protection mechanism with caps/conditions. Claims must arise from real estate transactions and are subject to statutory limits.

options.a: Ads need the agent's name and phone number, while the broker's name is optional
options.b: Ads must comply with TREC advertising rules, including required broker identification
options.c: Ads must show the agent's license number, while broker identification is required only on signs
options.d: Ads on social media are exempt from TREC rules if posted on a personal account

distractorExplanations.a: TREC rules make the broker's name mandatory in advertising; omitting it is the most common advertising violation.
distractorExplanations.c: TREC requires broker identification in all advertising, not just signs; license numbers are not the required element.
distractorExplanations.d: Social media posts advertising brokerage services are advertising under TREC rules, including broker identification.

options.a: Act only if the offense occurred before the license was issued
options.b: Discipline the license, including suspension or revocation
options.c: Refer the case to the Recovery Trust Account and take no license action
options.d: Wait for the next renewal to review it, with no action before then

distractorExplanations.a: TREC may act on relevant convictions that occur after licensing too; licensees must report them.
distractorExplanations.c: The Recovery Trust Account pays consumer judgments; it is not a substitute for disciplinary action.
distractorExplanations.d: TREC does not have to wait for renewal; it can open a disciplinary case once it learns of the conviction.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-license-l.explanation: Criminal history/conduct can trigger TREC disciplinary action under TRELA. Action is taken under TRELA and TREC's criminal-history guidelines.

options.a: Is satisfied by the 180 pre-licensing hours, so no SAE or CE is due at renewal
options.b: Must be completed as required for renewal (including SAE and CE as applicable)
options.c: Requires 30 hours of CE every year, with no separate SAE course requirement
options.d: Can be waived for active agents who close at least 10 transactions a year

distractorExplanations.a: Pre-licensing hours earn the first license only; Texas requires SAE for the first renewal and CE thereafter.
distractorExplanations.c: Texas uses SAE (98 hours) for the first renewal and 18 CE hours per two-year period, not 30 hours yearly.
distractorExplanations.d: Transaction volume does not waive TREC education requirements for renewal.

options.a: TREC has adopted a mandatory form for that transaction type and an exception does not apply
options.b: The listing agent's brokerage has not adopted its own in-house contract template for that sale
options.c: A Texas REALTORS® association form covers that transaction type, so it may be used instead of TREC's
options.d: The buyer uses mortgage financing, since cash purchases may use any form

distractorExplanations.b: Brokerages cannot substitute in-house templates for a promulgated form; the duty to use TREC forms does not depend on this.
distractorExplanations.c: Association forms are for situations without a promulgated form; they cannot replace a mandatory TREC form.
distractorExplanations.d: Promulgated form use does not depend on financing; cash sales of resale homes also use the TREC contract.

options.a: Right to terminate during the option period only for inspection-related defects
options.b: Unrestricted right to terminate during the option period for a negotiated fee
options.c: Right to extend the closing date by 30 days in exchange for the negotiated fee
options.d: Right to terminate if financing fails, with the fee credited toward closing costs

distractorExplanations.a: The TREC termination option is unrestricted; the buyer need not cite inspection defects or any reason.
distractorExplanations.c: The option fee buys a termination right, not a closing extension; extensions require an amendment.
distractorExplanations.d: Termination for failed financing comes from the Third Party Financing Addendum, not the option paragraph.

options.a: The same payment as the option fee, paid directly to the seller
options.b: Required consideration without which the TREC contract is unenforceable
options.c: Not consideration required to form the contract but a contractual deposit
options.d: A deposit the listing broker keeps in the operating account until closing

distractorExplanations.a: The option fee and earnest money are separate payments with different purposes in the TREC contract.
distractorExplanations.b: Mutual promises are the consideration; a contract can be valid even if earnest money is not deposited.
distractorExplanations.d: Earnest money goes to the named escrow agent or a trust account, never the broker's operating account.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Earnest money supports performance remedies; option fee is separate if used. It is usually held by the escrow agent named in the contract.

options.a: Adding warranty language or legal remedies the parties want beyond the form
options.b: Modifying the default and termination paragraphs so they favor the licensee's own client
options.c: Disclosing the seller's known defects instead of using the disclosure notice
options.d: Factual business details not addressed elsewhere—not for unauthorized legal drafting

distractorExplanations.a: Adding legal warranties or remedies is legal drafting, which licensees may not do in Special Provisions.
distractorExplanations.b: Rewriting form paragraphs is prohibited legal drafting; Special Provisions is for factual business details.
distractorExplanations.c: Known defects belong in the Seller's Disclosure Notice; Special Provisions does not replace it.

options.a: Written or oral agreement stating the agency relationship
options.b: The conduct of the parties, which implies the relationship over time
options.c: A licensee's delivery of the IABS notice at the first substantive contact
options.d: A cooperating broker's acceptance of a commission split at closing

distractorExplanations.b: Agency arising from conduct is implied agency, the opposite of express agency.
distractorExplanations.c: The IABS informs consumers about brokerage services; delivering it does not create an agency relationship.
distractorExplanations.d: Who pays or shares compensation does not by itself create express agency; an agreement does.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Express agreements create agency; ostensible/implied agency can arise from conduct—risky without disclosure. A written listing agreement is the most common example.

options.a: Obedience, loyalty, disclosure, and confidentiality owed to both parties equally
options.b: Obedience, loyalty, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting, and reasonable care
options.c: Honesty and fair dealing, the same duties owed to every customer
options.d: Loyalty and confidentiality, but no duty to disclose known material facts

distractorExplanations.a: Fiduciary duties run to the client; the other party is a customer owed honesty and fair dealing.
distractorExplanations.c: Honesty and fair dealing are duties to all parties; clients are owed the fuller fiduciary duties.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure of material facts is a core fiduciary duty, so omitting it describes the duties incorrectly.

options.a: Optional unless the buyer requests it in writing before the option period
options.b: Completed by the listing agent from the agent's own walkthrough
options.c: Required to be provided by the seller with known material defects
options.d: Required only for homes built before 1978, as part of lead disclosure

distractorExplanations.a: The notice is required by statute for most resale homes, whether or not the buyer requests it.
distractorExplanations.b: The notice states the seller's knowledge; licensees should not complete it on the seller's behalf.
distractorExplanations.d: That confuses the seller's disclosure notice with the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Texas Property Code requires seller disclosure in many residential transfers; licensees should not fill it for the seller as if they were the seller. Texas Property Code section 5.008 lists statutory exceptions.

options.a: Replacement of the original parties by a new agreement
options.b: Recording the executed contract in county records
options.c: Termination of the contract by mutual release
options.d: Transfer of contract rights to another party

distractorExplanations.a: Replacing parties or obligations by a new agreement is novation, not assignment.
distractorExplanations.b: Recording gives public notice; it does not transfer contract rights to another party.
distractorExplanations.c: A mutual release ends the contract; assignment keeps it alive with a new holder of the rights.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Assignment transfers rights; novation replaces parties/obligations with consent. Assignment is subject to any limits in the contract.

options.a: At first contact with another party to a proposed transaction
options.b: When an offer is submitted, through the contract's broker information section
options.c: At first contact with a party, but only if that party asks about it
options.d: Before closing, by noting the relationship on the settlement statement

distractorExplanations.b: The broker information section confirms representation later; TRELA requires disclosure at first contact.
distractorExplanations.c: Disclosure is required at first contact whether or not the other party asks.
distractorExplanations.d: Settlement-statement timing is far too late; representation must be disclosed at first contact.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Texas requires timely disclosure of representation. TRELA requires this disclosure of representation.

options.a: An open listing, where the broker is paid only on performance
options.b: A typical purchase contract where both parties make promises
options.c: An option contract, where the optionor alone is bound to perform
options.d: A reward offer for a buyer referral, accepted by performing the act

distractorExplanations.a: An open listing is a classic unilateral contract: the seller promises payment only if the broker performs.
distractorExplanations.c: An option binds only one party (the optionor), which makes it the textbook unilateral example.
distractorExplanations.d: Acceptance by performance rather than a return promise is the definition of a unilateral contract.

options.a: A ready, willing, and able buyer is procured by the listing broker, but not if the seller finds the buyer
options.b: A ready, willing, and able buyer is procured during the listing term, even if the seller finds the buyer
options.c: The property is shown by the broker at least once during the term, whoever finds the eventual buyer
options.d: A buyer is procured within the protection period after expiration, but not during the listing term

distractorExplanations.a: Excluding seller-found buyers describes an exclusive agency listing, not exclusive right-to-sell.
distractorExplanations.c: Showing the property does not earn a commission; a ready, willing, and able buyer must be procured.
distractorExplanations.d: The protection period extends the broker's right after expiration; it does not replace the listing term.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell usually entitles the broker to commission regardless of who finds the buyer. Exact terms follow the listing agreement.

options.a: Represents both parties after oral consent and must personally negotiate for each side
options.b: Represents both parties with written consent and may appoint associates under the rules
options.c: Acts as a common-law dual agent, without written consent from either party
options.d: Must appoint the same associate to work with both parties and give each party opinions on price

distractorExplanations.a: Intermediary status requires written consent from both parties, and the broker may appoint associates.
distractorExplanations.c: Texas replaced undisclosed dual agency with intermediary rules that require written consent.
distractorExplanations.d: Appointed license holders are different associates, one per party; one associate cannot advise both.

options.a: A customer relationship in which the broker owes the buyer only honesty
options.b: An agency relationship in which the broker represents the buyer as a client
options.c: A subagency relationship in which the broker represents the seller
options.d: An intermediary relationship in which the broker serves both the buyer and the seller

distractorExplanations.a: A signed buyer representation agreement makes the buyer a client with fiduciary duties, not a customer.
distractorExplanations.c: Subagency means working for the seller through the listing broker, the opposite of buyer representation.
distractorExplanations.d: Intermediary status needs written consent from both parties; a buyer agreement alone creates buyer agency.

options.a: Earnest money is deposited with the listing broker, who holds it in the trust account
options.b: Earnest money is typically deposited with the escrow agent as the contract specifies
options.c: Earnest money is paid to the seller at signing and credited to the buyer at closing
options.d: Earnest money is deposited with the lender once the buyer's loan application is filed

distractorExplanations.a: The TREC 1-4 contract names an escrow agent (usually the title company) to receive earnest money, not the listing broker.
distractorExplanations.c: Earnest money is held in escrow, not paid to the seller, so it can be refunded or forfeited under the contract.
distractorExplanations.d: The lender is not the escrow agent; the contract names the escrow agent that holds earnest money.

options.a: Title company closing with executed documents and lender funding
options.b: Attorney-only closings, since Texas bars title companies from closing
options.c: The listing broker preparing the settlement statement and disbursing funds
options.d: Recording the deed first, with lender funding up to 30 days afterward

distractorExplanations.b: Texas closings are commonly handled by title companies; attorney-only closing is the rule in some other states.
distractorExplanations.c: Brokers do not act as settlement agents; the title company prepares statements and disburses funds.
distractorExplanations.d: Funding and recording happen together at closing; the deed is not recorded weeks before funding.

options.a: FHA loan LTV exceeds 80%, since FHA loans carry PMI rather than MIP
options.b: Conventional LTV exceeds lender threshold (commonly above 80%)
options.c: Conventional LTV exceeds 90%, while 80–90% LTV needs no coverage
options.d: The borrower's debt-to-income ratio exceeds 43% on a loan

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans carry MIP (mortgage insurance premium), not PMI; PMI applies to conventional loans.
distractorExplanations.c: The common PMI trigger is an LTV above 80%, not 90%.
distractorExplanations.d: PMI is triggered by loan-to-value, not by the debt-to-income ratio.

options.a: Express the note interest rate alone, excluding the lender's points and other fees
options.b: Express the total cash the borrower must bring to closing
options.c: Express the yearly cost of credit including certain fees for comparison
options.d: Express the monthly payment including principal, interest, taxes, and insurance

distractorExplanations.a: APR adds certain finance charges to the interest rate; the note rate alone is not APR.
distractorExplanations.b: Cash to close is shown on the Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure; it is not the APR.
distractorExplanations.d: PITI is a monthly payment figure; APR is an annual cost-of-credit percentage.

options.a: Final loan approval after the appraisal and title commitment are cleared
options.b: A prequalification based on the borrower's stated income, without any document review
options.c: A binding loan commitment that locks the interest rate and terms through closing
options.d: Conditional lender assessment of borrower creditworthiness subject to underwriting

distractorExplanations.a: Final approval (clear to close) comes after underwriting; a preapproval is conditional.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes prequalification; preapproval involves verified credit and income documents.
distractorExplanations.c: Preapproval is neither a binding commitment nor a rate lock; both come later.

options.a: Property taxes and HOA dues between buyer and seller as of closing
options.b: The buyer's loan origination fees between buyer and seller as of closing
options.c: The listing commission between buyer and seller by days of ownership
options.d: The earnest money between buyer and seller according to the closing date

distractorExplanations.b: Origination fees are a buyer loan cost, not a prorated item tied to the ownership period.
distractorExplanations.c: The listing commission is a seller charge under the listing agreement; it is not prorated.
distractorExplanations.d: Earnest money is credited to the buyer at closing; it is not split by ownership days.

options.a: Show final loan terms at least three business days before closing
options.b: Help consumers understand loan costs early in the application process
options.c: Confirm the lender's final loan approval and list the clear-to-close conditions
options.d: Disclose the settlement agent's title charges after closing occurs

distractorExplanations.a: That is the Closing Disclosure; the Loan Estimate comes within three business days of application.
distractorExplanations.c: The Loan Estimate is an early cost disclosure, not a loan approval or clear-to-close notice.
distractorExplanations.d: The Loan Estimate is given early in the process, not after closing.

options.a: Are prepaid interest to reduce the note rate, typically 1% of the sales price per point
options.b: Are lender fees that raise the APR but leave the note rate unchanged
options.c: Are prepaid interest to reduce the note rate, typically 1% of loan amount per point
options.d: Are a one-time PMI premium, typically 1% of the loan amount per point

distractorExplanations.a: A point is 1% of the loan amount, not the sales price.
distractorExplanations.b: Discount points buy down the note rate; fees that leave the rate unchanged are origination charges.
distractorExplanations.d: Points are prepaid interest, not mortgage insurance premiums.

options.a: Originate loans directly to borrowers through retail branches
options.b: Insure lenders against borrower default on high loan-to-value loans
options.c: Set the federal funds rate that drives mortgage interest rates
options.d: Buy loans from originators, increasing liquidity for new lending

distractorExplanations.a: Originating loans is the primary market; the secondary market buys loans already made.
distractorExplanations.b: Default insurance on high-LTV loans is private mortgage insurance, not the secondary market's role.
distractorExplanations.c: The Federal Reserve sets the federal funds target; Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy loans.

options.a: Liens, easements, and other claims affecting title
options.b: The buyer's credit report and loan approval terms
options.c: The property's appraised value and comparables
options.d: Seller-disclosed defects in the home's condition

distractorExplanations.b: Credit and loan terms are lender underwriting items, not title encumbrances.
distractorExplanations.c: Value comes from the appraisal; a title commitment reports claims affecting title.
distractorExplanations.d: Physical defects appear in the seller's disclosure and inspection, not the title commitment.

options.a: The option period ends without the buyer delivering a notice of termination to the seller
options.b: Lender wires funds and recording/closing conditions are met per the transaction
options.c: The buyer receives the Closing Disclosure three business days before closing
options.d: The lender issues a loan commitment letter after underwriting approval

distractorExplanations.a: The end of the option period removes a termination right; it does not fund the purchase.
distractorExplanations.c: The Closing Disclosure is a pre-closing notice; funding happens later when the lender wires money.
distractorExplanations.d: A commitment letter precedes closing; funding needs the actual wire and satisfied closing conditions.

options.a: Via judicial foreclosure in state district court, as required for all mortgages
options.b: Via nonjudicial trustee sale when power of sale exists, subject to notice rules
options.c: Via strict foreclosure, vesting title in the lender without a public sale
options.d: Via a sheriff's sale after a court judgment, then a one-year redemption period

distractorExplanations.a: Judicial foreclosure is required in some states, but Texas deeds of trust usually allow nonjudicial sale.
distractorExplanations.c: Strict foreclosure is used in a few states; Texas uses public trustee sales with notice.
distractorExplanations.d: Texas trustee sales on residential deeds of trust have no general one-year redemption period.

options.a: Are lender fees that increase the note rate
options.b: Are prepaid interest used to buy down the note rate
options.c: Are origination fees that leave the rate unchanged
options.d: Are prepaid property taxes held in escrow at closing

distractorExplanations.a: Discount points lower the note rate; they do not raise it.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes origination charges; discount points buy down the rate.
distractorExplanations.d: Escrowed property taxes are prepaids, not discount points.

options.a: The buyer's owner's title insurance premium
options.b: Ad valorem property taxes for the current year
options.c: The seller's mortgage payoff balance at closing
options.d: The broker's commission based on days of ownership

distractorExplanations.a: In Texas the title premium is paid by the party the contract names; it is not prorated by days.
distractorExplanations.c: The seller's payoff is a seller debit, not an item split between buyer and seller.
distractorExplanations.d: Commission is set by the listing agreement and is not prorated.

options.a: Lender against covered title defects up to the loan balance
options.b: Owner/insured against covered title defects up to the policy amount
options.c: Owner against structural defects in the home up to the policy amount
options.d: Owner against new liens arising after the policy date

distractorExplanations.a: That describes the lender's (mortgagee) policy, not the owner's policy.
distractorExplanations.c: Title insurance covers title defects, not the physical condition of the house.
distractorExplanations.d: Title policies cover defects existing at the policy date, not later liens.

options.a: Exceeds the conforming loan limit and is held in the lender's portfolio
options.b: Meets Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac purchase guidelines (including size limits)
options.c: Is insured by FHA and meets HUD's county loan limits
options.d: Is backed by a VA guaranty and requires no down payment

distractorExplanations.a: Loans above the conforming limit are jumbo (nonconforming) loans.
distractorExplanations.c: FHA loans are government loans; conventional loans have no FHA insurance.
distractorExplanations.d: VA loans are government-backed, not conventional conforming loans.

options.a: Land plus improvements and appurtenances
options.b: Land plus trade fixtures and growing crops
options.c: Land and buildings, excluding easements
options.d: Improvements only, without the land itself

distractorExplanations.b: Trade fixtures and annual crops (emblements) are generally personal property, not real property.
distractorExplanations.c: Appurtenances such as easements are part of real property and pass with the land.
distractorExplanations.d: Real property starts with the land; improvements alone are not the full definition.

options.a: A street address and the appraisal district account number written into the deed
options.b: Metes and bounds, recorded plat (lot/block), or rectangular survey where used
options.c: The MLS listing description together with the property's tax parcel number
options.d: Metes and bounds only, since Texas does not use recorded plat maps

distractorExplanations.a: Addresses and tax account numbers are informal identifiers, not adequate legal descriptions.
distractorExplanations.c: MLS text and parcel numbers can change and do not legally fix the boundaries.
distractorExplanations.d: Texas widely uses recorded plats (lot and block); metes and bounds is not the sole method.

options.a: Public use and the owner's written consent to sell the property
options.b: Just compensation paid at the property's assessed tax value
options.c: A zoning change approved by the city council after a public hearing
options.d: Public use/purpose and just compensation (condemnation process)

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is a forced taking; owner consent is not required, only just compensation.
distractorExplanations.b: Just compensation is based on fair market value, not the tax assessment.
distractorExplanations.c: Zoning is police power regulation; eminent domain is a taking with compensation.

options.a: Property received by gift or inheritance during marriage becomes community property
options.b: Most property acquired during marriage is owned equally by spouses, with exceptions
options.c: Each spouse owns marital property in proportion to the income each contributed to it
options.d: Spouses hold property acquired during marriage as tenants by the entirety

distractorExplanations.a: Gifts and inheritances are separate property in Texas, even if received during marriage.
distractorExplanations.c: Community property is owned in undivided equal halves, not by income contribution.
distractorExplanations.d: Texas does not recognize tenancy by the entirety; it is a community property state.

options.a: An adjacent dominant tenement rather than a particular person or company
options.b: The servient estate owner who grants others access across the land
options.c: A person or company (e.g., utility) rather than a dominant parcel
options.d: A landlocked neighbor who gains access across the parcel by necessity

distractorExplanations.a: Benefiting a dominant parcel describes an easement appurtenant, not an easement in gross.
distractorExplanations.b: The servient owner is burdened by the easement, not the party it benefits.
distractorExplanations.d: An easement by necessity benefits a parcel, so it is appurtenant rather than in gross.

options.a: Race, color, religion, sex, age, marital status, and national origin (federal)
options.b: Race, religion, sex, disability, source of income, and national origin (federal)
options.c: Race, color, religion, and national origin, as listed in the 1866 Civil Rights Act
options.d: Race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, and national origin (federal)

distractorExplanations.a: Age and marital status are not federal Fair Housing Act classes; disability and familial status are.
distractorExplanations.b: Source of income is not a federal protected class; it appears only in some state or local laws.
distractorExplanations.c: The 1866 Act covers race only; the Fair Housing Act list also includes sex, disability, and familial status.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Federal Fair Housing Act protected classes are core; Texas/local may add protections. State and local laws may add further protected classes.

options.a: Housing built before 1978 generally requiring pamphlet/disclosure
options.b: Housing built before 1980 generally requiring a lead inspection
options.c: Housing built before 1978, but only when the seller knows of lead
options.d: Commercial buildings built before 1978 that are open to the public

distractorExplanations.b: The cutoff is 1978, and the rule requires disclosure and a pamphlet, not a mandatory inspection.
distractorExplanations.c: The pamphlet and disclosure form are required for pre-1978 housing even if the seller knows of no lead.
distractorExplanations.d: The federal lead disclosure rule covers residential target housing, not commercial buildings.

options.a: Is free of all liens and easements, with no exceptions in the policy
options.b: Is reasonably free from significant defects that would deter a prudent buyer
options.c: Is conveyed by general warranty deed, even with serious recorded defects
options.d: Has been insured by a title company at a prior sale of the property

distractorExplanations.a: Marketable title can still have minor exceptions; it must be free of defects that would deter a prudent buyer.
distractorExplanations.c: The deed type does not make title marketable; serious defects still make it unmarketable.
distractorExplanations.d: A past policy does not prove current marketability; title is examined for each sale.

options.a: A trade fixture a tenant installed for business use in a leased storefront
options.b: A right or improvement that runs with the land, such as an easement appurtenant
options.c: An easement in gross held personally by a utility company for its overhead power lines
options.d: A neighbor's license to cross the land, which the owner may revoke at will

distractorExplanations.a: Trade fixtures remain the tenant's personal property and do not run with the land.
distractorExplanations.c: An easement in gross benefits a person or company, not a parcel, so it is not appurtenant.
distractorExplanations.d: A license is a revocable personal privilege, not a right that runs with the land.

options.a: The county appraisal district through property tax assessments and penalties
options.b: Private parties such as HOAs or benefitted landowners through civil action
options.c: TREC through license discipline against the agent who sold the restricted lot
options.d: The county clerk who records the restrictions in the deed records

distractorExplanations.a: Appraisal districts value property for taxes; they do not enforce private deed restrictions.
distractorExplanations.c: TREC regulates license holders; deed restrictions are private covenants enforced in court.
distractorExplanations.d: The clerk only records documents; recording does not mean the clerk enforces them.

options.a: Property acquired during marriage is generally separate property unless both spouses sign the deed
options.b: Property acquired during marriage is generally community property unless it is separate property
options.c: Texas applies community property rules only to the homestead, not other real property
options.d: Inherited property received during marriage becomes community property once it is recorded

distractorExplanations.a: That reverses the Texas presumption: acquisitions during marriage are presumed community property.
distractorExplanations.c: Community property rules cover all property acquired during marriage, not just the homestead.
distractorExplanations.d: Inheritances are separate property; recording does not convert them to community property.

options.a: An unpaid mechanic's lien recorded against the property by a contractor
options.b: A structure or improvement crossing a boundary line onto another's land
options.c: The property's flood insurance premium for the coming year
options.d: The appraised value of the improvements relative to the land

distractorExplanations.a: Recorded liens are found by a title search, not by a physical boundary survey.
distractorExplanations.c: A survey may show the flood zone, but the premium is set by the insurer.
distractorExplanations.d: Value allocation comes from an appraisal, not an encroachment survey.
